'''Papua New Guinea Premier Soccer League''' is the men's top division of professional [[association football|soccer]] in [[Papua New Guinea]]. Formed in 2006 as the '''National Soccer League''' by the [[Papua New Guinea Football Association]], it replaced the [[Papua New Guinea National Club Championship]] as the country's major soccer competition, and was renamed the Premier Soccer League in 2022.<ref name="abc2022rename">{{Cite web |date=2022-05-29 |title=Premier Soccer League set to kick off under a cloud in Papua New Guinea, with champions Lae City absent and FA critics' voices growing louder {{!}} ABC |url=https://www.abc.net.au/pacific/programs/pacificbeat/png-soccer/102545182 |access-date=2022-05-04 |language=en-US}}</ref>

[[PNG Hekari FC|Hekari United]] have won ten editions of the competition, while [[Lae City F.C.|Lae City]] have won seven; the two clubs have met in two grand finals, in [[2015–16 Papua New Guinea National Soccer League|2015–16]] and [[2019 Papua New Guinea National Soccer League|2019]], with Lae City winning both.<ref name=":14" /> [[Gulf Komara F.C.|Komara Gulf]] are the reigning champions, having won their first title in [[2025 Papua New Guinea Premier Soccer League|2025]].<ref name="rsssfchamp">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesp/pngchamp.html|title=Papua New Guinea - List of Champions|website=[[RSSSF]]|access-date=2018-05-22}}</ref> The [[2026 Papua New Guinea Premier Soccer League|2026 season]] has been contested by 12 teams.<ref name="rsssf2026">{{Cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesp/png2026.html |title=Papua New Guinea 2026 |website=[[RSSSF]] |access-date=2026-07-25}}</ref>

== History ==
=== Foundation ===
The National Soccer League was started by [[David Chung (football executive)|David Chung]], the President of the [[Papua New Guinea Football Association]] (PNGFA), in 2006. It was the first nationwide semi-professional football league, and a step up from the amateur [[Papua New Guinea National Club Championship]], which had been in existence since 1976.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesp/png06.html|title=Papua New Guinea 2006|website=[[RSSSF]]|access-date=2018-05-22}}</ref> In the first season, the semi-professional and amateur champions played a two-legged playoff to decide that year's qualifier for the [[OFC Champions League]].<ref name=":0" />

Since its inception, with the exception of the 2015–16 season, it has consisted of an initial league phase, with each team playing other twice, before the top four teams enter a knockout championship playoff, with the eventual league champion decided in a one-legged grand final.

=== 2006–2012: Early years and Hekari dominance ===
The first eight editions of the competition were won by [[PNG Hekari FC|Hekari United / PNG Hekari FC]], under different names.<ref name=":14">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesp/pngchamp.html|title=Papua New Guinea - List of Champions|website=[[RSSSF]]|access-date=2018-05-22}}</ref> In [[2006 Papua New Guinea National Soccer League|2006]], five teams entered the competition from five different provinces: [[Port Moresby]] (PRK Souths United), [[Lae]] ([[Morobe FC|TL Blue Kumuls]]), [[Central Province (Papua New Guinea)|Central Province]] ([[Gelle Hills United|Gelle Hills]]), [[Madang Province|Madang]] ([[Madang FC|Madang Flying Fox]]) and [[Mount Hagen District|Mount Hagen]] ([[Welgris Highlanders|Welgris Momads]]).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.oceaniafootball.com/archives-4729/|title=PNGFA – HISTORIC LANDMARK AS PNGNSL GETS UNDERWAY|date=20 October 2006 |publisher=Oceania Football Confederation|language=en-US|access-date=2018-06-02}}</ref> A sixth side, to come from Lae, [[Kimbe]] or [[Autonomous Region of Bougainville|Bougainville]], eventually did not enter.<ref name=":0" /> PRK Souths United won, defeating Gelle Hills 2–0 in the Grand Final. However, they failed to qualify for the OFC Champions League after a 4–2 aggregate defeat to amateur side [[University Inter F.C.|University Inter]] in the Overall Final.<ref name=":0" />

The [[2007–08 Papua New Guinea National Soccer League|2007–08 season]] was played in late 2007 and early 2008, and became known as the Telikom NSL Cup, due to sponsorship reasons.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesp/png07.html|title=Papua New Guinea 2007|website=[[RSSSF]]|access-date=2018-05-22}}</ref> All five of the founding members entered once again, albeit under various names: TL Blue Kumuls became Morobe FC; Welgris Momads became Welgris Highlanders; PRK Souths United became Hekari United; and Madang Flying Fox became simply Madang Fox. Furthermore, two new teams entered, [[Rapatona F.C.|Rapatona FC]] and [[Besta Madang Fighters|Besta Madang]].<ref name=":1" /> The top four teams in the regular season qualified for the Championship playoffs, with Hekari United finishing top of the regular season and defeating Gelle Hills in the final again.<ref name=":1" />

In the [[2008–09 Papua New Guinea National Soccer League|2008–09 season]], the league was expanded to eight teams, albeit with three from the previous season not taking part. Madang Fox and Besta Madang withdrew, while Gelle Hills application was rejected in favour of a new tem [[Sepik FC]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesp/png08.html|title=Papua New Guinea 2008|website=[[RSSSF]]|access-date=2018-05-22}}</ref> Also joining the league were [[Eastern Stars F.C.|Eastern Stars]], [[Nabasa United]] and University Inter. Hekari and Inter were first and second in the regular season table, but it was Hekari and Rapatona who were due to meet in the Grand Final; however, following postponements on 21 March and 28 March, the PNGFA awarded the championship and qualification to the OFC Champions League to Hekari United by virtue of their higher league position.<ref name=":2" />

The [[2009–10 Papua New Guinea National Soccer League|2009–10 season]] saw the league expanded once again, to encapsulate nine teams. Sepik FC withdrew after failing to submit a letter of interest, while Welgris Highlanders missed the application deadline.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesp/png09.html|title=Papua New Guinea 2009|website=[[RSSSF]]|access-date=2018-05-22}}</ref> Nabasa United also withdrew, while Gelle Hills and Madang Fox were reinstated. There were new entries from [[Tukoko University Lae FC|Tukoko University FC]] and [[Besta United PNG|Besta PNG United]], the latter of which acted as the national U-20 squad. Hekari United again finished top of the regular season table, and played Gigira Laitepo in the Grand Final, winning 5–0.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/hekari-rock/|title=Hekari rock|date=2010-04-25|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-22|language=en-US}}</ref>

For the first time since its inception, the number of teams decreased ahead of the [[2010–11 Papua New Guinea National Soccer League|2010–11 season]], with Gelle Hills, Rapatona FC and University Inter all withdrawing, while [[Petro Souths F.C.|Petro Souths FC]] joined the league for the first time.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesp/png2011.html|title=Papua New Guinea 2010/11|website=[[RSSSF]]|access-date=2018-05-22}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/petro-souths-join-nsl/|title=Petro Souths join NSL|date=2010-07-07|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-22|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/eight-for-nsl/|title=Eight for NSL|date=2010-07-13|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-22|language=en-US}}</ref> That left seven sides taking part, with Hekari finishing the season unbeaten and top of the league, defeating Eastern Stars 4–0 in the final.<ref name=":4" />

The [[2011–12 Papua New Guinea National Soccer League|2011–12 season]] saw relative stability within the league, with only one side (Madang Fox) withdrawing, being replaced by new entrants [[Bulolo United]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/bulolo-utd-fc-seek-the-best-for-nsl/|title=Bulolo Utd FC seek the best for NSL|date=2011-08-18|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-22|language=en-US}}</ref> Hekari United once again finished top of the regular season and played Eastern Stars in the Grand Final for the second consecutive season, winning 3–0.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesp/png2012.html|title=Papua New Guinea 2011/12|website=[[RSSSF]]|access-date=2018-05-22}}</ref>

In July 2012, PNGFA president and league founder David Chung was named as a recipient of the [[Order of the British Empire]] in the [[Queen's Birthday Honours]] list.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://boxscorenews.com/ofc-president-receives-order-of-the-british-empire-honour-p40732-68.htm|title=OFC President receives Order of the British Empire honour|website=boxscorenews.com|access-date=2018-05-23}}</ref>

=== 2013–2016: Difficulties and disillusionment ===
[[2013 Papua New Guinea National Soccer League|2013]] saw a delay. By late December 2012, only four teams had completed the registration process: defending champions Hekari United, Besta United PNG, Welgris Highlanders, returning from a three-year absence, and newcomers [[WNB Tavur|West New Britain Tavur]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/former-nsl-boss-critical-of-late-start/|title=Former NSL boss critical of late start|date=2012-12-23|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-22|language=en-US}}</ref> Another new franchise, [[FC Port Moresby]], joined in early January.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/fc-pom-in-nsl/|title=FC Pom in NSL|date=2013-01-06|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-22|language=en-US}}</ref> The NSL had decided to go ahead with the league with just six teams, the lowest since the inaugural season. Morobe FC and [[NC Civil Works Oro FC]], submitted their registration on the same day.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/nsl-face-dilemma-on-sixth-team/|title=NSL face dilemma on sixth team|date=2013-01-09|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-22|language=en-US}}</ref> This led to Hekari United's owner, [[John Kapi Natto]], urging the NSL to re-adjust the league to cater for all teams.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/nsl-urged-to-adjust-format/|title=NSL urged to adjust format|date=2013-01-13|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-22|language=en-US}}</ref> It was on 29 January that the teams were confirmed, with the addition of Eastern Stars.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/lupari-confirms-nsl-eight/|title=Lupari confirms NSL eight|date=2013-01-29|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-22|language=en-US}}</ref>

The NSL board took further criticism from new side WNB Tavur. The NSL contractually paid for the travel costs, but were unwilling to cover the more expensive travel costs.<ref name=":5">{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/tavur-blame-nsl-board/|title=Tavur blame NSL board|date=2013-02-17|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-22|language=en-US}}</ref> This led to Tavur playing three consecutive away matches, to avoid back and forth travel costs.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesp/png2012a.html|title=Papua New Guinea 2012/13|website=[[RSSSF]]|access-date=2018-05-22}}</ref> The season concluded on 1 June, with Hekari United claiming their seventh consecutive title, winning 3–0 against FC Port Moresby in the Grand Final.<ref name=":6" />

The [[2014 Papua New Guinea National Soccer League|2014 season]] initially had 12 interested teams,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/pay-up-nsl-tells-teams/|title=Pay up, NSL tells teams|date=2013-10-16|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-22|language=en-US}}</ref> but by 21 October, only seven had completed the registration process, including new sides [[Admiralty Palaiau FC|Admiralty FC]] and [[Lae F.C.|Lae FC]]. The previous season's finalists FC Port Moresby had not done so, and neither had last year's debutants WNB Tavur.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/moresby-yet-to-sign-up-for-nsl/|title=Moresby yet to sign up for NSL|date=2013-10-21|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-22|language=en-US}}</ref> Both ended up excluded from the competition, with FC Port Moresby eventually lodging an appeal.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/nsl-back-on-the-menu/|title=NSL back on the menu|date=2014-01-01|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-22|language=en-US}}</ref> This led to another delay, with the start date being postponed three times<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/nsl-in-limbo/|title=NSL in limbo|date=2014-01-29|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-22|language=en-US}}</ref> before eventually starting on 8 February, after FC Port Moresby withdrew their case.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/nsl-season-set/|title=NSL season set|date=2014-02-04|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-22|language=en-US}}</ref> In April 2014, Morobe FC's owner Tuguyawini Libe Parindali accused the National Soccer League of being ''too expensive'', claiming that there was ''no incentive'' to keep competing in the division.<ref name=":7">{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/%E2%80%98nsl-is-too-expensive%E2%80%99/|title='NSL is too expensive'|date=2014-04-07|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-22|language=en-US}}</ref> This was in response to the NSL's decision to stop subsidising airfares, accommodation, food and transport for away games, something they had done since the inception of the league in 2006.<ref name=":7" />

On the pitch, Hekari United were awarded their eighth consecutive league title on 24 May 2014, despite the Grand Final being abandoned after 70 minutes due to crowd violence.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesp/png2014.html|title=Papua New Guinea 2014|website=[[RSSSF]]|access-date=2018-05-22}}</ref> With Hekari leading 3–0, several Lae FC fans started throwing stones, with Hekari goalkeeper [[Godfrey Baniau]] being hit several times.<ref name=":8">{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/disgust-reigns-at-lae-soccer-supporter%E2%80%99s-behaviour/|title=Disgust reigns at Lae soccer supporter's behaviour|date=2014-05-26|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-22|language=en-US}}</ref> Some claimed that the referee was biased towards Hekari United, with the decision to send off Lae captain [[Kohu Liem]] causing the outrage, while others blamed the organisers who failed to clear supporters who had not paid for the event.<ref name=":8" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/soccer-sector-riddled-with-controversies/|title=Soccer sector riddled with controversies|date=2014-05-30|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-22|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/disruption-at-grand-final-was-because-of-referee/|title=Disruption at grand final was because of referee|date=2014-05-28|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-26|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/crowd-violence-mars-final/|title=Crowd violence mars final|date=2014-05-26|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-26|language=en-US}}</ref>

Ahead of the [[2015 Papua New Guinea National Soccer League|2015 season]], Gigira Laitepo, who had sponsored Morobe FC for the entirety of their eight-year league history, withdrew their sponsorship throwing the franchise into disarray.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/franchise-in-dilemma/|title=Franchise in dilemma|date=2014-09-09|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-22|language=en-US}}</ref> The club ended up withdrawing from the league, as did Eastern Stars and [[Lae FC]]. Toti City F.C., a new franchise under similar management to the previous year's runners-up, took the place of Lae, while FC Port Moresby returned, as did Madang FC after a three-year absence.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/bidding-time-ends-for-franchises-in-nsl/|title=Bidding time ends for franchises in NSL|date=2014-07-30|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-22|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":9">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesp/png2015.html|title=Papua New Guinea 2015|website=[[RSSSF]]|access-date=2018-05-22}}</ref>

The season became the first in history that Hekari didn't win the title; the eight-time champions were beaten by Madang FC in the semi-finals of the playoffs, despite finishing the regular season top of the table. Madang went on to lose 5–1 to Toti City in the final, with the Lae club winning the title after just two years of existence.<ref name=":9" /> The [[2015–16 Papua New Guinea National Soccer League|2015-16 season]] saw unprecedented interest, with 12 teams successfully signing up, and the organisers taking a decision to split the division into two zones, northern and southern. New teams included [[PS Huawei]], [[Erema FC]], [[Goroka Gosiha]] and Rapatona FC, the latter of whom was returning to the competition after a five-year absence.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/four-new-sides/|title=Four new sides|date=2015-10-23|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-22|language=en-US}}</ref> Morobe FC, now under the sponsorship of Welgris, also returned. The top two teams from each zone entered a second group stage, and the top two teams facing off once again in the final. For the second season in a row, Toti City won the title, ahead of Hekari United, winning 2–0.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesp/png2016.html|title=Papua New Guinea 2015/16|website=[[RSSSF]]|access-date=2018-05-22}}</ref>

=== 2017–2018: League split ===
Towards the end of 2016, several cumulative events triggered many clubs across Papua New Guinea to split from the PNGFA-organised National Soccer League, eventually forming a rival association, the [[Football Federation Papua New Guinea]] (FFPNG).<ref name=":10">{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/pngfa-gives-kapi-natto-boot/|title=PNGFA gives Kapi Natto the boot|date=2016-11-30|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-23|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/mobiha-condemns-sacking/|title=Mobiha condemns sacking|date=2016-12-02|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-23|language=en-US}}</ref> On 29 December 2016, Chung was re-elected as president of the association.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/pngfa-returns-chung/|title=PNGFA returns Chung|date=2016-12-29|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-23|language=en-US}}</ref> The following day, Kapi Natto declared that Hekari United, along with 11 of the 18 other associations affiliated with the PNGFA, would be pulling out of the upcoming National Soccer League season.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/hekari-pulls-nsl-ofc-comp/|title=Hekari pulls out of NSL, OFC comp|date=2016-12-30|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-23|language=en-US}}</ref>

On 2 February 2017, Hekari were disqualified from the [[2017 OFC Champions League]] after the PNGFA filed a complaint.<ref name=":11">{{Cite news|url=https://www.oceaniafootball.com/hekari-united-disqualified/|title=Hekari United disqualified|date=2017-02-02|publisher=Oceania Football Confederation|access-date=2018-05-23|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/hekari-ousted/|title=Hekari ousted|date=2017-02-03|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-23|language=en-US}}</ref> The ruling claimed that by making derogatory statements regarding the PNGFA, as well as several players failing to report for international duty, the club had ''engaged in behaviour that damaged the integrity of football''.<ref name=":11" /> Despite this, NSL competition manager Simon Koima maintained that Hekari's participation in the [[2017 Papua New Guinea National Soccer League|2017 National Soccer League]] was still possible,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/door-open-hekari/|title=Door open for Hekari|date=2017-02-08|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-23|language=en-US}}</ref> but on 27 February, Kapi Natto launched the Football Federation Papua New Guinea and its flagship competition, the [[Papua New Guinea National Premier League|National Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/new-body-launched/|title=New body launched|date=2017-02-27|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-23|language=en-US}}</ref> The 2017 National Soccer League kicked off in May, with only 4 teams from the previous season remaining: Lae City Dwellers, Madang FC, PS Huawei and Besta PNG United. New sides included [[Buang FC]] and [[Southern Strikers]].<ref name=":12">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesp/png2017.html|title=Papua New Guinea 2017|website=[[RSSSF]]|access-date=2018-05-23}}</ref> The season was riddled with difficulties, beginning with new side Southern Strikers withdrawing without playing a match.<ref name=":12" /> They were replaced by [[Vitis Yamaros FC]]. After several deferred and even cancelled matches, the season was set to conclude with the playoffs in August.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/nsl-board-set-dates-playoff-matches/|title=NSL board to set dates for playoff matches|date=2017-08-03|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-23|language=en-US}}</ref> However, PS Huawei disbanded before their rearranged playoff semi-final, while the NSL cancelled the Grand Final.<ref name=":12" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/pacific/337520/sport-png-s-national-soccer-league-playoffs-cancelled|title=Sport: PNG's National Soccer League playoffs cancelled|date=2017-08-18|work=Radio New Zealand|access-date=2018-05-25|language=en-nz}}</ref> Lae City Dwellers were declared champions, having maintained the best regular season record.

The [[2018 Papua New Guinea National Soccer League|2018 season]] started with Southern Strikers successfully replacing Vitis Yamaros FC, while many (aside from disbanded PS Huawei) remained in the division, alongside new sides [[F.C. Morobe Wawens|FC Morobe Wawens]] and [[FC Momase]]. Lae City Dwellers were renamed Toti City Dwellers for sponsorship reasons.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://oceaniafc.com/can-lae-city-dwellers-reach-oceania-champions-league-final|title=Can Lae City Dwellers reach the Oceania Champions League final?|website=oceaniafc.com|language=en-US|access-date=2018-05-23}}</ref>  In early January, the PNGFA was banned from using all PNG Sports Foundation facilities due to outstanding payments from the [[2016 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup]], which took place in the country.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/pngfa-banned-facilities/|title=PNGFA banned from facilities|date=2018-01-15|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-23|language=en-US}}</ref> On May 3, it was decided that all the remaining matches were to be forfeited, as only four sides – Toti City, Besta PNG United, Morobe Wawens and Madang – had paid their affiliation fee in full.<ref name=":13">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesp/png2018.html|title=Papua New Guinea 2018|website=[[RSSSF]]|access-date=2018-05-23}}</ref> However, by the following week, Southern Strikers settled their fee, and their remaining matches were rescheduled, while Buang and Momase had 0–3 defeats awarded in the remaining fixtures.<ref name=":13" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/deferred-nsl-matches-get-nod/|title=Deferred NSL matches get nod|date=2018-05-11|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-23|language=en-US}}</ref>

Following investigations into corruption, David Chung stepped down from all roles on 6 April.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.oceaniafootball.com/ofc-president-steps-down/|title=OFC President steps down|date=2018-04-06|publisher=Oceania Football Confederation|access-date=2018-05-23|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.pngfootball.com.pg/pngfa-president-steps-down/|title=PNGFA President steps down|date=2018-04-10|work=PNGFootball.com.pg|access-date=2018-05-23|language=en-US}}</ref> Members of both the PNGFA and the FFPNG agreed to hold talks regarding the league split and other issues surrounding the sport in the country.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/federation-association-agree-sort-issues-affecting-soccer/|title=Federation, association agree to sort out issues affecting soccer|date=2018-04-13|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-23|language=en-US}}</ref> In the Grand Final, Toti City Dwellers defeated Besta PNG United 3–0 on 26 May to win their fourth straight title.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/city-hammer-united-claim-3rd-title/|title=City hammer United to claim 3rd title|date=2018-05-28|work=The National|access-date=2018-05-28|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.pngfootball.com.pg/toti-city-reigns-claiming-third-title/|title=Toti City reigns claiming third title|date=2018-05-28|work=PNGFootball.com.pg|access-date=2018-06-01|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.oceaniafootball.com/third-straight-title-for-toti/|title=Third-straight title for Toti|date=2018-05-29|publisher=Oceania Football Confederation|access-date=2018-06-01|language=en-US}}</ref>

=== 2019–2021: League reunification and COVID-19 ===
On 27 October 2018, after over 18 months of division within the sport domestically, the PNGFA and the FFPNG reunited, with John Kapi Natto becoming the new president.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/soccer-unites/|title=Soccer unites|date=2018-10-29|work=The National|access-date=2018-10-29|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.oceaniafootball.com/pngfa-elects-new-president/|title=PNGFA elects new President|date=2018-10-29|publisher=Oceania Football Confederation|access-date=2018-10-29|language=en-US}}</ref> Plans for the [[2019 Papua New Guinea National Soccer League|2019 season]] were announced in November 2018, with the expectation of four separate regions: Southern ([[Papua Region|Papua]]), Northern ([[Momase Region|Momase]]), [[Highlands Region|Highlands]] and [[Islands Region|Islands]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pngfootball.com.pg/national-soccer-league-calls-for-expression-of-interest-from-clubs/|title=National Soccer League calls for expression of interest from clubs|date=2018-11-20|website=PNGFootball.com.pg|language=en-US|access-date=2019-03-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/competition-looking-at-nationwide-participation/|title=Competition looking at nationwide participation|date=2018-11-19|website=The National|language=en-US|access-date=2019-03-24}}</ref> The competition kicked off on 26 January 2019, with a record 27 teams taking part across all regions of the country.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://postcourier.com.pg/nsl-set-kick-off-january-26/|title=NSL set to kick off on January 26|date=2019-01-18|website=Post Courier|language=en-US|access-date=2019-03-24}}</ref> On 30 March, [[Laiwaden F.C.|Laiwaden FC]] goalkeeper [[Mikes Gewa]] was kicked in the ribs by Morobe Wawens' [[Jason Farrock]], and the player was hospitalised.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesp/png2019.html|title=Papua New Guinea 2019|website=[[RSSSF]]|access-date=2019-05-17}}</ref> The player died under a month later.<ref name="postcourier.com.pg">{{Cite web|url=https://postcourier.com.pg/players-death-sends-shockwaves-soccer-circles/|title=Player's death sends shockwaves through soccer circles|date=2019-05-01|website=Post Courier|language=en-US|access-date=2019-05-17}}</ref> It was revealed that the National Soccer League hadn't taken out [[Health insurance|medical insurance]] to cover its players.<ref name="postcourier.com.pg"/> The format of the playoffs caused controversy,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/format-irks-fans-officials/|title=Format irks fans, officials|date=2019-05-15|website=The National|language=en-US|access-date=2019-05-17}}</ref> mainly because teams from the same regional division were not kept apart until the final. Furthermore, the format was changed twice within a month, leading Eastern Stars' chairman [[Joseph Ealedona]] to describe it as ''fraud at the highest level''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://postcourier.com.pg/nsl-finals-draw-change-ticks-off-franchises/|title=NSL finals draw change 'ticks off' franchises|date=2019-05-15|website=Post Courier|language=en-US|access-date=2019-05-17}}</ref> PNGFA chairman Kapi Natto responded to the criticism by distancing the association from the management of the NSL, and stating that he believed the draws were done after taking into consideration the costs involved.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://postcourier.com.pg/nsl-testing-new-ground/|title=NSL testing new ground|date=2019-05-16|website=Post Courier|language=en-US|access-date=2019-05-17}}</ref> Nevertheless, the playoffs continued, and the two previous champions, Hekari United and Toti City, ended up meeting in the Grand Final. Following a goalless scoreline after 120 minutes, Toti City won their fifth consecutive title, winning 5–4 overall.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://postcourier.com.pg/toti-city-win-title-thriller/|title=Toti City win title in thriller|date=2019-06-03|website=Post Courier|language=en-US|access-date=2019-06-08}}</ref>

The start of the [[2019–20 Papua New Guinea National Soccer League|2019–20 season]] was delayed several times, having originally planned an expansion to include a two-tier system, with a national Premier Division and a regional Conference Division.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oceaniafootballcenter.home.blog/2019/10/13/png-national-soccer-league-plans-two-tier-expansion/|title=PNG National Soccer League Plans Two-Tier Expansion|date=2019-10-13|website=Oceania Football Center|language=en|access-date=2019-12-31|archive-date=2019-10-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191014071716/https://oceaniafootballcenter.home.blog/2019/10/13/png-national-soccer-league-plans-two-tier-expansion/|url-status=dead}}</ref> However, lack of interest led to the cancellation of the Conference Division,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oceaniafootballcenter.home.blog/2019/11/27/planned-png-conference-competition-cancelled-due-to-lack-of-interest/|title=Planned PNG 'Conference Competition' cancelled due to lack of interest|date=2019-11-27|website=Oceania Football Center|language=en|access-date=2019-12-31|archive-date=2019-11-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191128091734/https://oceaniafootballcenter.home.blog/2019/11/27/planned-png-conference-competition-cancelled-due-to-lack-of-interest/|url-status=dead}}</ref> and a ten-team competition was announced on 10 December.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oceaniafootballcenter.home.blog/2019/12/10/10-team-png-nsl-kicks-off-this-weekend/|title=10-Team PNG NSL kicks off this weekend|date=2019-12-10|website=Oceania Football Center|language=en|access-date=2019-12-31|archive-date=2019-12-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191210124920/https://oceaniafootballcenter.home.blog/2019/12/10/10-team-png-nsl-kicks-off-this-weekend/|url-status=dead}}</ref> The season was completed despite an enforced five-month break due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Papua New Guinea|COVID-19 pandemic]], with Lae City picking up their sixth title after a 1–0 victory over [[Vitiaz United F.C.|Vitiaz United]] in the grand final.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-10-11|title=Lae City Claim Sixth Title After Professional and Polished Performance against Vitiaz|url=https://oceaniafootballcenter.org/2020/10/11/lae-city-claim-sixth-title-after-professional-and-polished-performance-against-vitiaz/|access-date=2020-12-28|website=Oceania Football Center|language=en}}</ref> The [[2021 Papua New Guinea National Soccer League|2021 season]] was also delayed, originally scheduled to begin on July 17.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-02 |title=NSL attracts 13 clubs for '21 season {{!}} The National |url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/nsl-attracts-13-clubs-for-21-season/ |access-date=2025-05-04 |language=en-US}}</ref> The season was ultimately abandoned without a champion being crowned, amid a resurgence of COVID-19 cases in the country.<ref name="national2021abandon">{{Cite news |title=PNGFA awaits response |url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/pngfa-awaits-response/ |work=The National |date=2021-10-20 |access-date=2026-07-25}}</ref>

=== 2022–present: Rebranding and the Premier Soccer League era ===
The competition returned in October 2022, played across five regional conferences — Southern, Northern, Highlands, New Guinea Islands Central and New Guinea Islands Eastern — a structure last used in 2015–16.<ref name="rsssf2022">{{Cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesp/png2022.html |title=Papua New Guinea 2022 |website=[[RSSSF]] |access-date=2026-07-25}}</ref> The playoff series, postponed from its original December 2022 date, concluded in February 2023 with Lae City beating Hekari United 5–3 on penalties after a 1–1 draw, claiming their seventh domestic title.<ref name="rsssf2022" /> Both grand finalists subsequently met in a two-legged play-off to decide Papua New Guinea's [[2023 OFC Champions League]] representative; Hekari United won 4–1 on aggregate to claim the berth, despite having lost the domestic final.<ref name="rsssf2022" />

In May 2022, the competition was rebranded as the '''Papua New Guinea Premier Soccer League'''.<ref name="abc2022rename" /> The first season played under the new name ran from July to December 2023 with eight clubs, and was won by Hekari United, who beat newcomers Lae City Dwellers 1–0 in the grand final.<ref name="rsssf2023">{{Cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesp/png2023.html |title=Papua New Guinea 2023 |website=[[RSSSF]] |access-date=2026-07-25}}</ref> Hekari United retained the title in [[2024 Papua New Guinea Premier Soccer League|2024]], beating Gulf Komara 2–1 in the grand final, before Gulf Komara won their maiden title in [[2025 Papua New Guinea Premier Soccer League|2025]], defeating FC Morobe Wawens 3–1.<ref name="rsssfchamp" />

Ahead of the [[2026 Papua New Guinea Premier Soccer League|2026 season]], the PNGFA registered 12 clubs — the most in the competition's history — including four newcomers, and long-time champions Hekari United rebranded as '''PNG Hekari FC'''.<ref name="sportstok2026launch">{{Cite web |last=Kei |first=Jonah |title=PSL Launched 20th Edition |url=https://www.sportstokmagazine.com/post/psl-launched-20th-edition |website=Sports Tok Magazine |date=2026-05-29 |access-date=2026-07-25}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-29 |title=PSL 2026 Officially Launched {{!}} The National |url=https://www.facebook.com/pngfa2020/posts/-psl-2026-officially-launched-the-premier-soccer-league-2026-season-was-official/1539254461544294/ |access-date=2026-05-04 |language=en-US}}</ref> PNG Hekari finished last in the inaugural [[2026 OFC Professional League]] before returning to the domestic competition.<ref>{{cite web |title=We start the Premier League season with a win today over Madang United FC today at the PNG Football Stadium|url=https://www.facebook.com/permalink.php?story_fbid=pfbid0BwdtAsTAFAj28tD9NUZJEKY5RficdHsgSmQobgYVgeMwq9SDMwzyHGUovXYoATdWl&id=61580327264204 |publisher=Facebook |access-date=5 June 2026}}</ref> The season was launched on 28 May 2026 in Port Moresby and began on 30 May, with the regular season played as a double round-robin, ahead of a knockout playoff series.<ref name="national2026launch">{{Cite news |last=Kig |first=Robertlyn |title=PSL launches season with expanded line-up |url=https://www.thenational.com.pg/psl-launches-season-with-expanded-line-up/ |work=The National |date=2026-06-01 |access-date=2026-07-25}}</ref>

== Format ==
The competition's structure has varied considerably across its history. In most seasons it has consisted of a league phase, in which participating clubs play each other at least once, followed by a knockout series among the top four placed teams, comprising semi-finals, a third-place play-off, and a one-legged grand final.<ref name=":0" /> Notable exceptions include the 2015–16 season, which used a two-zone system culminating in a top-two play-off;<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesp/png2016.html|title=Papua New Guinea 2015/16|website=[[RSSSF]]|access-date=2018-05-22}}</ref> the 2019 season, contested across four regional divisions by a record 27 clubs;<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://postcourier.com.pg/nsl-set-kick-off-january-26/|title=NSL set to kick off on January 26|date=2019-01-18|website=Post Courier|access-date=2019-03-24}}</ref> and the 2022 season, which reverted to a five-conference regional format.<ref name="rsssf2022" /> Since the Premier Soccer League rebrand, the competition has generally featured a single national division of 8 to 12 teams.<ref name="rsssf2023" /> The winner, and in some seasons the runner-up, qualified for the [[OFC Champions League]].<ref name=":0" />

== Sponsorship ==
The league has been known under various sponsorship names throughout its history. The 2007–08 season was sponsored as the Telikom NSL Cup.<ref name=":1" /> From 2019, the competition was known as the Kumul Petroleum Holdings Limited National Soccer League, or KPHL National Soccer League, for sponsorship reasons.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://postcourier.com.pg/kumul-petroleum-takes-naming-rights-nsl/|title=Kumul Petroleum takes naming rights to NSL|date=2019-01-31|work=Post Courier|access-date=2019-06-30}}</ref> As of the 2026 season, the competition had no confirmed title sponsor.<ref name="sportstok2026launch" />

== Teams ==
{{main|2026 Papua New Guinea Premier Soccer League#Teams}}
12 teams contested the 2026 season, drawn primarily from Port Moresby and Lae, with further representation from Kerema, Madang, Milne Bay Province, Manus Province and Finschhafen District.<ref name="rsssf2026" /> The number of participants has fluctuated considerably across the competition's history, from a low of five in the inaugural 2006 season, to a high of 27 spread across four regions in 2019.<ref name=":0" />
